subject: Genetics
title: CCR5-Delta32 and the Plague
description: A quick win: understand CCR5-Delta32 and the Plague.

hook.text: A 32-base deletion in the CCR5 gene makes you resistant to HIV. About 10% of Europeans carry it.

buildup.text: CCR5 is a receptor HIV uses to enter cells. Delete 32 bases, the receptor is malformed, and HIV can't dock.

discovery.text: The mutation is rare outside Europe. Scientists asked: what selected for it? The leading theory: the Black Death.

twist.text: Recent research challenges this. Smallpox may have been the real driver. The debate continues in genetics labs.

climax.text: An ancient plague may have gifted modern Europeans resistance to a virus that wouldn't exist for centuries.

punchline.text: A medieval plague left a genetic gift against a modern virus.

quiz.question: What does the CCR5-Delta32 mutation do?
